data.narrative:
Dendra Systems is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Susan Graham and Irina Fedorenko, having raised $18M to date. The Climate & Energy sector includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen, though none qualify as sufficiently proximate comparables on stage, timing, and valuation tier.

Given the thinness of narrow-stage peer data in this sector, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $18M capital proxy yields a $36M implied valuation. This method is applicable where peer comps are unavailable; the multiplier reflects median progression patterns across venture-backed climate and energy companies moving from Series A to subsequent rounds.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $31M to $41M, with a median of $36M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression anchor. Key uncertainties include the absence of transaction comparables at identical stage and sector positioning—the available peer set spans multiple stages and valuations—and limited visibility into Dendra's specific capital efficiency and revenue trajectory relative to the broader Climate & Energy cohort. A subsequent valuation refinement would benefit from either narrower peer identification or disclosure of company-specific unit economics and customer concentration metrics.
